text.p: Copa America hosts Bolivia, making the most of their advantage of playing at 3,600 metres above sea level, beat Uruguay 1-0 Wednesday to complete their group matches with maximum points and without conceding a goal.

Bolivia finished top of group B to join second-placed Peru, who earlier beat Venezuela 2-0, in the quarter-finals. Defending champions Uruguay were third with three points and will have to wait until Thursday's final group C matches to know if they go through as one of the two best of the three third-placed teams.
The result also qualified Paraguay, who finished third in group A with four points, one more than Uruguay.

Julio Cesar Baldivieso scored the only goal in the 30th minute when the Uruguayan defence left him unmarked at a corner, giving him time to trap the ball on his chest, dribble past goalkeeper Roberto Siboldi and fire the ball into the empty net.

Bolivia dominated the match, missed an incredible number of chances and struck the woodwork three times in the second half of an entertaining match. Siboldi performed heroics throughout to keep the score down.

Uruguay, who are going through a bad patch in international soccer, showed spurts of energy but clearly suffered in the thin air. Bolivia's players beat them to almost every loose ball, even when the Uruguayan players seemed clear favourites to get there first.
Bolivia had faced public apathy at the start of the tournament, playing their first two games in a one-third full stadium with high ticket prices partially blamed.
Organisers decided to allow two people in for the price of one for Wednesday's game and were rewarded with a crowd of around 35,000 in the 45,000-capacity stadium.
The home players appeared to appreciate the atmosphere and played with far more spirit than before.
Bolivia will meet the second best third-placed team in their semi-final in La Paz on Saturday while Peru face Argentina, who finished second in group A, in Sucre the same day.
Bolivia's win averted a crisis which could have hit the competition if they had finished second in the group.

Argentina threatened to pull out over an alteration in the rules made on Tuesday when the Copa America organisers announced that if Bolivia finished second, their quarter-final against the second-placed group A team -- which turned out to be Argentina -- would be moved to La Paz.
The match had originally been scheduled for Sucre, which at 2,700 metres above sea level is only 100 metres higher than Argentina's first round venue Cochabamba.
Argentine coach Daniel Passarella was so angry at the change that he threatened to take his team back to Buenos Aires rather than play in the thin air of La Paz.
